edits.before: Include the time first noticed, any change in the wet area, staining or swelling, and whether the supply has been isolated. A wide photo can show the location; a closer photo can show the visible detail. Take both without disturbing finishes or approaching electrical hazards. Previous repairs, recent plumbing work and an unusual water bill are useful context, but none proves the cause on its own.
edits.after: Include the time first noticed, any change in the wet area, staining or swelling, and whether the supply has been isolated. Photos are optional: a wide photo can show the location and a closer photo the visible detail, without disturbing finishes or approaching electrical hazards. Water can travel before it becomes visible, so a photo records symptoms and access rather than establishing the source. Previous repairs, recent plumbing work and an unusual water bill are useful context, but none proves the cause on its own.
edits.reason: Merge the photo/source explanation into the substantive observation chapter

edits.before: If the meter is safely accessible and the situation is stable, note the meter type, readings and times. Water Corporation's household leak-check guidance compares ordinary meter readings after actual water use has stopped for 15 minutes. An integrated smart meter uses its own model instructions and usage display; do not apply the ordinary dial-reading method to every meter.
edits.after: You can request an inspection without meter readings. If the meter is safely accessible and the situation is stable, note the meter type, readings and times. Water Corporation's household leak-check guidance compares ordinary meter readings after actual water use has stopped for 15 minutes. An integrated smart meter uses its own model instructions and usage display; do not apply the ordinary dial-reading method to every meter.
edits.reason: Keep optional meter readings with the existing stable-leak/meter explanation
